evals.name: classify-residue-shapes-with-tiers
evals.prompt: Audit code comments for residue: read evals/fixtures/residue-snippet.py relative to the skill directory and classify what you find.
evals.expected_output: Emits a per-file tier table: the 'used to batch writes … now flushes' comment as history-narration (Tier 1), the 'as you asked' comment as conversational-antecedent (Tier 1), the 'Task 2 replaces the old …' comment as plan-reference (Tier 1), and the 'see PR #45' comment as ticket-pr-residue (Tier 2), each with delete/review treatment guidance. No edits are applied.
expectations: Output classifies findings by the skill's shape vocabulary (history-narration, plan-reference, conversational-antecedent, ticket-pr-residue)
The 'used to … now flushes' comment is flagged as history-narration
The 'see PR #45' comment is flagged as ticket-pr-residue at Tier 2
The output is a classification report with tiers and treatments; no file is edited

evals.name: read-only-even-when-asked-to-fix
evals.prompt: Run comment-residue on src/parser.py and just delete the residue comments you find — strip them for me.
evals.expected_output: Stays read-only despite the request to edit: surfaces the findings with treatment guidance and does NOT apply Edit/Write. It explains the author applies each deletion, or points to /code-tidying:tidy for the edit-capable pass.
expectations: Output does NOT edit or write the file despite the explicit request to strip comments
Output surfaces findings with treatment guidance for the author to apply
The read-only contract is honored or explicitly stated

evals.name: sanctioned-todo-not-flagged
evals.prompt: Audit a file whose only tracker reference is `# TODO(#123): switch to CRC32 once the format is frozen`. Classify it.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes TODO(#issue) as the sanctioned back-reference and does NOT flag it as ticket-pr-residue. Only bare provenance references (see PR #, from branch, JIRA-123) are ticket residue.
expectations: The TODO(#123) line is NOT flagged as ticket-pr-residue
Output states that TODO(#issue) tracking real work is the sanctioned exception

evals.name: code-word-not-in-comment-not-flagged
evals.prompt: Audit a file with the line `previously = load_cache()` — 'previously' is an identifier in code, not a comment. Classify it.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT flag the code identifier as history-narration: residue detection runs only on the comment portion of a line, so a residue-shaped word in an identifier or string literal is never flagged.
expectations: The `previously` identifier in code is NOT flagged as history-narration
Output states that detection is scoped to the comment portion of a line

evals.name: not-delete-all-comments
evals.prompt: Audit a file with `# Sums the payload bytes modulo 2**32.` above the code. Flag it.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT flag a legitimate present-tense why/what-it-can't-express comment. Only the five residue shapes are findings; a comment that carries non-obvious intent or a contract stays.
expectations: The legitimate present-tense comment is NOT classified as any residue shape
Output distinguishes residue from comments worth keeping (non-obvious why / interface intent)

evals.name: markdown-is-audit-noise-not-comment-residue
evals.prompt: Run comment-residue on docs/notes.md — it contains 'used to do X, now does Y' narration. Flag it.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT audit the markdown file — code-comment residue is code-file-only; markdown noise is the sibling /audit-noise's territory. It reports no code targets and routes markdown to /audit-noise.
expectations: The .md file is not audited (no findings emitted for it)
Output routes markdown noise to /audit-noise rather than handling it here

evals.name: origin-notes-are-tier-1-findings
evals.prompt: Audit code comments for residue: read evals/fixtures/origin-notes.sh relative to the skill directory and classify what you find.
evals.expected_output: Emits exactly five origin-note findings at Tier 1, one per line naming where the block came from or when it was added ('ported from the melodic-software dotfiles profile', 'Merged 2026-07-24 from dot_bashrc', 'Added 2026-08-10 while wiring permission/hook telemetry', 'Copied from the provisioning repo and adapted for Windows', 'Backported 2026-09-01 from main'), each with a delete treatment because git history owns origin. Nothing else in the file is a finding. No edits are applied.
expectations: All five origin-note lines are classified as origin-note at Tier 1 with a delete treatment

The three license-header lines (Copyright, SPDX-License-Identifier, Licensed under the MIT License) are NOT flagged; a license or attribution header is exempt from this shape even when it carries an origin cue
None of the four dated stamp lines (verified, Checked, Confirmed, As of) is flagged: a dated stamp is load-bearing, not an origin note
The why-comment 'Must stay ordered because the parser reads the first match' is NOT flagged
The bare date line '2026-08-10' is NOT flagged: an origin verb is required
The 'TODO(#123): tighten the upper bound' marker is NOT flagged; a marker comment is exempt from this shape even when it carries an origin cue
The output is a classification report with tiers and treatments; no file is edited

evals.name: weak-history-cues-are-tier-2-and-wrapped-lines-join
evals.prompt: Audit a file with the comments `# keeps the order exactly as before`, `# now uses the old shared group`, and a wrapped pair `# grouped for speed (ci-perf Phase` / `# 6b) and nothing else`, plus `# phase 2 of the build parses the header`. Classify them.
evals.expected_output: Reports history-narration-weak at Tier 2 (Review, not Delete) for the 'exactly as before' comment, for the 'the old shared group' comment, and once for the wrapped 'Phase 6b' pair, at the first line's number. The 'phase 2 of the build' comment is not a finding. It explains the weak cues also open ordinary prose, which is why a person reviews them. No edits are applied.
expectations: 'exactly as before' and 'the old shared group' are classified as history-narration-weak at Tier 2 with a review treatment
The wrapped 'Phase 6b' comment is found once, at the line where it starts
The 'phase 2 of the build' comment is NOT flagged
Output explains that the weak cues can be ordinary prose, so they are reviewed rather than deleted
The output is a classification report with tiers and treatments; no file is edited

evals.name: workaround-without-link-or-removal-condition-is-flagged
evals.prompt: Audit a shell file with these comments and classify them: `# Workaround: the cache client drops the first write after a reconnect, so write twice.`, `# Workaround for the parser crash: https://example.org/bugs/88`, `# Workaround until the vendor SDK 4.2 ships: pin the v1 endpoint.`, `# Workaround for upstream issue #412.`, and the two-line comment `# Workaround: the IDE holds a lock on the output folder;` / `# remove when the IDE releases it after a build.` The file also has the code line `workaround_count=0`.
evals.expected_output: Reports one unjustified-workaround finding at Tier 2, on the cache-client comment, with a review treatment that names fixing the cause or adding a link or removal condition. The URL, 'until', and issue-number comments are not findings, the two-line comment is justified by its second line, the issue number is not reported as ticket-pr-residue, and the identifier workaround_count is not flagged. No edits are applied.
expectations: The cache-client comment is classified as unjustified-workaround at Tier 2 with a review treatment, not a delete treatment
The comments carrying a URL, 'until', or an issue number are NOT flagged as unjustified-workaround
The two-line comment is NOT flagged: the removal condition on its second line justifies the run
The 'upstream issue #412' comment is NOT reported as ticket-pr-residue, because a workaround's reference is its justification
The identifier workaround_count is NOT flagged
The output is a classification report with tiers and treatments; no file is edited

evals.name: added-since-reports-only-added-lines
evals.prompt:
/code-tidying:audit-comment-residue --added-since main

(The branch adds two lines to app.py: '# Workaround: write twice' and a code line. app.py already carried '# used to buffer writes' on line 1 before the branch, and lib.py is unchanged and also carries '# used to buffer writes'.)
evals.expected_output: Runs detect.sh with --added-since main and reports only the unjustified-workaround finding on the added comment in app.py. The history-narration comments on unchanged lines in app.py and in the unchanged lib.py are not reported, and lib.py is not audited. No question is asked and no edits are applied.
expectations: Runs detect.sh with --added-since main
Reports the unjustified-workaround finding on the added comment in app.py
Does NOT report the history-narration comment on app.py line 1 or the one in lib.py, since neither sits on an added line
Finishes the report without asking the user a question
No file is edited
